messages:
maria: Quick sync — I pushed a draft benchmark narrative + two chart variants to the shared drive. Need help finalizing framing for launch: one aimed at PLG engineers, one for sales/enterprise. TL;DR findings in the doc: ~30% lower median p95 latency at equivalent throughput and ~1.7x lower per-token cost on short-sequence chat workloads vs our baseline infra. Thoughts?

alex: Skimmed it. 👍 Re chart types: for PLG landing page we should avoid stacked bars. Engineers care about tail behavior — show a latency CDF and a small table with per-token cost. For blog/PR, a single simple chart that highlights cost-per-response is fine.

chris: Agreed on CDF. Also suggest an iso-cost vs latency scatter (each point = model+config) so you can show pareto-optimal configs. Call out 95th explicitly.

sam: Messaging split idea: PLG headline -> "Fast responses, predictable cost" with a CTA to try the hosted API. Enterprise headline -> "Predictable latency, SLA-ready capacity" with link to Dedicated/Private contact form and webinar sign-up.

lee: For inbound routing: recommend webhook on the webinar sign-up to create MQL in HubSpot. Then rule: if company_size > 50 AND expected_monthly_tokens > 10M -> assign to AE queue, else nurture via SDR + automated onboarding email. We should capture use-case (chat/embeddings/inference-only) on the form.

maria: @alex @chris good — for the PLG page I want a single hero stat (median latency on 128-token sequences) and a secondary line about cost-per-1k-tokens. For the blog we can expand to CDF + iso-cost chart. Sam — can you draft two headline variants?

sam: Drafts: 1) "Latency-first inference that doesn’t break the bank" (PLG). 2) "Predictable throughput and economics for production LLMs" (Enterprise). Quick A/B copy: shorter CTAs on PLG, a form gated asset (benchmark whitepaper) for enterprise.

chris: Minor nit: avoid absolute numbers without context. Instead of "1.7x cheaper" use phrasing like "up to 1.7x lower per-token cost on short sequences; results vary by model and config" — legal-friendly and accurate.

alex: For visuals: use these rules — hero: single metric + delta badge vs baseline; blog: CDF (log-scale x-axis optional), iso-cost scatter with annotations for our recommended configs; table: p50, p95, tokens/sec, cost-per-1k for 64/128/512 seq lengths.

maria: Good. Also thinking about a webinar to walk customers through the tradeoffs (batching, KV cache, quantization). Proposed title: "Serving LLMs: balancing latency and cost in production". Sam, can you run a 30/60/90 promotional plan and a landing page wire?

sam: On it. Promo plan in 48h. Landing wire: hero stat + 2-up chart (CDF + iso-cost) + registration form that asks company size and use-case.

lee: For lead scoring: add a tag if someone selects "private/on-prem" — route directly to Enterprise AE. Also include a boolean if they request SLA.

maria: One more: analytics tracking. Add custom events: "benchmark_download", "webinar_register", "try_endpoint_from_bench_page" — funnel end goes to marketing dashboard.

deploy-bot: [system] file uploaded: /shared/marketing/bench/drafts/bench-narrative-v3.pdf by maria at 2026-03-21 14:12:05 UTC

chris: Last item — visuals accessibility: ensure colorblind-safe palette and that the delta badges are paired with text (e.g., "+30% faster (median)").

alex: I'll mock the hero chart this afternoon and post screenshots. If everyone thumbs-up, we can lock copy by EOD Friday. :thumbsup:

maria: Perfect — thanks all. If you want to comment inline in the doc, do so. Otherwise we'll iterate on the two headline variants + the webinar landing flow and route rules.

lee: +1 — will draft the HubSpot workflow once landing wire is done.

sam: I'll throw the two headline variants + 3 CTA options into Figma and link back here when ready.

maria: Closing note — keep public messaging conservative: "up to" language, cite the test harness and baseline model versions in the blog. We'll include the raw data in the whitepaper for transparency.
